introduction-the-sensitive-brain.core: etcd holds all Kubernetes state and is sensitive: it needs low-latency disks (fsync per write), a stable network between members, quorum to accept writes, bounded database size (default quota 2 GB, max ~8 GB recommended) and regular compaction and defragmentation. Most 'Kubernetes is slow' incidents at scale trace back to etcd.

first_principles.problem: API calls slow to seconds, leader elections flap and the cluster becomes unstable.
truths: MVCC keeps old revisions until compacted.

analogy.title: The brain's memory centre
analogy.story: Fast and precise when healthy, but sleep deprivation (slow disks) makes everything else falter.
analogy.breaks: Brains self-heal overnight; etcd needs explicit maintenance.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: See leader, DB size and alarms per member.

code.text:
etcdctl endpoint status --cluster -w table
etcdctl endpoint health --cluster
etcdctl alarm list

check.q: Why does etcd need fast disks?
check.a: Every write is fsynced to its write-ahead log before acknowledgement, so disk latency directly limits throughput and stability.

defragmentation-cleaning-up-the-holes.core: etcd's MVCC keeps old revisions until compaction marks them free, but the bbolt database file doesn't shrink, leaving holes. Defragmentation rewrites the file to reclaim space, blocking the member during the operation. Run it member by member (followers first, leader last) when dbSize greatly exceeds dbSizeInUse, and clear any NOSPACE alarm afterwards.

first_principles.problem: etcd hits its space quota, raises a NOSPACE alarm and the cluster becomes read-only.

analogy.title: Defragmenting a filing cabinet
analogy.story: Shred old files (compaction), then reorganise drawers so the empty space is usable.
analogy.breaks: Cabinets stay usable during reorganising; a defragmenting member pauses requests.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: DB from 3.8 GB to 900 MB; writes resume.

code.text:
etcdctl endpoint status -w table             # dbSize vs in-use
etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd-2:2379 defrag
etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd-3:2379 defrag
etcdctl --endpoints=https://etcd-1:2379 defrag   # leader last
etcdctl alarm disarm

check.q: Why defragment etcd members one at a time?
check.a: Defrag blocks the member; doing them sequentially keeps quorum and availability.

member-management-surgery-on-the-cluster.core: Replacing or adding etcd members is surgery: always keep quorum. To replace a failed member, remove it (etcdctl member remove), then add the new one (member add) and start it with initial-cluster-state=existing. Add one member at a time, prefer learners (non-voting until caught up) and never run an even number long-term.

first_principles.problem: An engineer adds two new members at once to a 3-node cluster before they sync, and quorum is lost.

analogy.title: Replacing crew on a ship at sea
analogy.story: Swap one sailor at a time so there are always enough hands to sail.
analogy.breaks: Sailors can be trained on deck; etcd learners must replicate the full data set first.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Cluster back to 3 healthy voters without losing quorum.

code.text:
etcdctl member list
etcdctl member remove 8e9e05c52164694d
etcdctl member add etcd-3 --learner --peer-urls=https://10.0.3.10:2380
# start etcd-3 with --initial-cluster-state=existing, wait until caught up
etcdctl member promote <new-id>

check.q: What's the benefit of adding a new etcd member as a learner?
check.a: It replicates data without voting, so it can't affect quorum until it's caught up and promoted.

disaster-recovery-snapshots.core: etcd snapshots (etcdctl snapshot save) capture the full keyspace at a revision. Recovery from quorum loss or corruption restores the snapshot into a new data directory on each member (etcdutl snapshot restore with new cluster settings) and restarts a fresh cluster. Back up frequently, store off-cluster, encrypt and rehearse restores. Managed control planes do this for you.

first_principles.problem: Two of three control-plane disks fail and there's no recent etcd snapshot.
truths: Quorum loss can be unrecoverable without backups.
Snapshots are consistent points in time.
derivation: **Restore** to new data dirs on all members.

analogy.title: Saving the master ledger to a vault each hour
analogy.story: If the office burns down, you rebuild from the last vault copy.
analogy.breaks: Ledgers can be partially reconstructed; etcd restores everything to the snapshot point, losing later changes.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Cluster state rebuilt from the snapshot.

code.text:
etcdutl snapshot restore /backup/etcd-2026-10-18.db \
  --name etcd-1 --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restored \
  --initial-cluster etcd-1=https://10.0.1.10:2380,etcd-2=https://10.0.2.10:2380,etcd-3=https://10.0.3.10:2380 \
  --initial-cluster-token restored-1 --initial-advertise-peer-urls https://10.0.1.10:2380

check.q: What happens to changes made after the snapshot when you restore?
check.a: They're lost; the cluster returns to the snapshot's state.

monitoring-etcd-health-knowing-before-it.core: Key etcd metrics: etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds (p99 < 10 ms), etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds, etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total (should be rare), etcd_server_has_leader, etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_bytes vs quota, peer round-trip time and proposal failures. Alert on trends before they become outages.

first_principles.problem: etcd problems are only noticed when the API server starts timing out.
truths: Size grows toward a hard quota.

analogy.title: Vital signs monitoring
analogy.story: Rising temperature and irregular heartbeat warn before collapse.
analogy.breaks: Patients show symptoms; etcd often looks fine until it suddenly isn't, so alert early.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Disk issues caught before leader flapping.

code.text:
- alert: EtcdHighFsyncLatency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.01
  for: 10m
  labels: {severity: warning}
